findings.title: Deprecated TLS Protocol Version (TLS 1.0)
findings.evidence: Negotiated TLS 1.0 in ServerHello (Frame 23).
findings.why_it_matters: TLS 1.0 is formally deprecated by RFC 8996 and NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2. It lacks modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) and is vulnerable to attacks such as BEAST and POODLE.
findings.recommendation: Disable SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 across all mail services. Enforce TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only (e.g., 'smtpd_tls_mandatory_protocols = !SSLv2, !SSLv3, !TLSv1, !TLSv1.1').

findings.title: Insecure / Broken Cipher Suite (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA)
findings.evidence: Negotiated cipher suite 'TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA' contains broken primitive (3DES, DES) in Frame 23.
findings.why_it_matters: Cipher suite contains 3DES, DES, which is cryptographically broken and prohibited by NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 and RFC 7465/7590 due to plaintext recovery vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Remove broken ciphers from server configuration. Enforce modern AEAD suites such as ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256, ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

findings.why_it_matters: User credentials (usernames/passwords) were transmitted in plain text over the network without TLS encryption, exposing them to interception and credential theft.
findings.recommendation: Enforce TLS before permitting authentication. In Postfix configure 'smtpd_tls_auth_only = yes'; in Dovecot configure 'disable_plaintext_auth = yes'.

findings.title: STARTTLS Advertised But Not Utilized
findings.evidence: Server advertised STARTTLS capability in Frame 64, but client proceeded in cleartext.
findings.why_it_matters: The mail server offered opportunistic TLS upgrade, but communication remained in cleartext. This leaves traffic vulnerable to passive eavesdropping or STRIPTLS downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendation: Require TLS for client submissions on port 587/465. For inter-server mail, deploy MTA-STS (RFC 8461) and DANE (RFC 7672) to enforce encryption.
